summary:
La segunda **Punta Tech Week** se armó alrededor de la 18.ª edición del Punta Tech Meetup, que en 2026 cumplió su "mayoría de edad" con el lema "Let's Tech Together!". El evento central fue el lunes 12 de enero en los jardines del Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Atchugarry (MACA), con más de 2000 asistentes de más de 30 países. El primer Punta Tech Meetup, hace 18 años, reunía a unas 50 personas. La semana sumó alrededor de 40 side events en distintos puntos de Punta del Este (encuentros temáticos, after offices, cumbres sectoriales), además de un cóctel de bienvenida y la cuarta edición de W Meetup, un espacio para mujeres.

Lo organizan Carolina Kind y Bruno Gadea (de la productora Lucero), Pablo Brenner y Sergio Fogel (cofundador de dLocal). Fiel a su formato de pocas charlas y mucho networking, el escenario tuvo a Paula Bellizia, vicepresidenta de Amazon Web Services para América Latina, y una entrevista del periodista de la BBC Elliott Gotkine al ministro de Economía, Gabriel Oddone, que destacó el acuerdo entre la Unión Europea y el Mercosur. Asistieron la vicepresidenta Carolina Cosse, Guibert Englebienne (cofundador de Globant) y fondos como Riverwood Capital y Kaszek.

description:

La Global Game Jam 2026 tuvo en Uruguay su sede principal en el **Club del Emprendedor del Parque Tecnológico del LATU**, organizada por Jam2Jam, la Universidad ORT Uruguay e Ingenio del 30 de enero al 1.º de febrero. Jam2Jam festejó ahí sus cinco años organizando jams, con más de 300 jammers y casi 100 juegos acompañados. Según sus números, a esta edición fueron 74 participantes, y en 2026 las mujeres llegaron a un récord del 28 % de sus participantes. La transmisión de apertura muestra como auspiciantes a Ironhide Game Studio, Great Oak, DMoizo y Monster Energy.

El tema mundial fue «máscara» (*Mask*). En la sede del LATU se hicieron Disguise, Mask Maze, Everyone Needs Faces, BackStage, Buscando a Momo, Michelle, who?, De cara al lago y Chin-Chin!.

description:

SwissLedger is a Swiss institutional blockchain designed for regulated use cases across banking, industry and public administration. It evolved from Lugano’s city-level blockchain initiatives into a national-scale infrastructure, with governance, security and compliance built in by design.

In this session, Lorenzo will outline SwissLedger’s public-permissioned Proof of Authority (PoA) model, consortium governance and compliance-ready architecture. He will also present real-world use cases already in production, including Verify Lugano for document authenticity and notarisation, as well as financial sector applications such as tokenisation and programmable finance.
After the talk, the meetup will follow the standard LF Decentralized Trust European Chapter agenda, including short updates from members and ongoing initiatives, followed by open discussion.
This session is relevant for professionals interested in institutional adoption of blockchain and regulated distributed ledger technology.

title: AIA: An Open-Source Semantic Framework for Universally Interpretable Impact Data
description:
Climate and sustainability projects generate vast amounts of impact data — but too often, that data is hard to compare, integrate, or audit. Different projects use different terms, schemas, and structures — even when they are measuring the same underlying phenomena. This fragmentation creates friction for integrators and limits meaningful, global, cross-platform impact accounting.

On 17 February 2026 at 08:00 AM Pacific, the LFDT CA2-SIG Standards Working Group will present the [Anthropogenic Impact Accounting (AIA) ontology suite](https://www.lfdecentralizedtrust.org/blog/climate-action-official-release-of-the-anthropogenic-impact-accounting-ontology-suite), an open-source semantic framework designed to address this challenge. Developed over four years through rigorous bi-weekly working sessions and multiple redrafting cycles, the AIA suite provides a coherent and extensible foundation for expressing impact data in a universally interpretable way.

The first public release of AIA, published on 16 September 2025, comprises four modular, W3ID-registered ontologies:
\- claimont \([https://w3id.org/claimont](https://w3id.org/claimont)): Semantics for claims, claimants, evidence, and attestations
\- infocomm \([https://w3id.org/infocomm](https://w3id.org/infocomm)): Communication primitives for structured information exchange
\- impactont \([https://w3id.org/impactont](https://w3id.org/impactont)): Foundational concepts for modeling impact relationships
\- aiao \([https://w3id.org/aiao](https://w3id.org/aiao)): An integrated framework for anthropogenic impact accounting

Join us for an overview of how AIA can help your impact data become more interoperable, auditable, and reusable!

title: Workshop: CREDEBL For Decentralized Identity and Verifiable Credentials
description:
As adoption of Decentralized Identity (DID) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) accelerates across governments, education, enterprises, and regulated industries, developers and organizations need open, interoperable, and production-ready infrastructure to build trusted digital ecosystems.

This webinar introduces [CREDEBL](https://github.com/credebl/), an LF Decentralized Trust project, and walks participants through how to get started quickly, understand the architecture, and explore real-world use cases - all backed by open standards and community-driven development.

Whether you are a developer, architect, policy stakeholder, system integrator, or ecosystem partner, this session will help you move from concepts to implementation.

**What We’ll Cover**

* The Problem: Fragmented Digital Trust : Why identity, credentials, and verification remain siloed - and how this limits interoperability, privacy, and adoption.
* The Foundation: Verifiable Credentials & Decentralized Identity : A brief overview of DIDs, VCs, DIDComm, OID4VC, trust frameworks and where CREDEBL fits within the LFDT ecosystem.
* The Platform: CREDEBL Architecture : Core components, issuer–holder–verifier flows, APIs, and deployment models.
* Getting Started Fast: One-Click / Minimal-Config Setup : Live walkthrough of setting up CREDEBL and running end-to-end credential flows.
* Live Demo: Issuance & Verification in Action : Creating DIDs, issuing credentials, wallet interactions, and verification scenarios.
* Real-World Adoption & Ecosystem Use Cases : Education, digital identity, enterprise and public-sector use cases.
* Community, Governance & Roadmap : Open-source contribution model, roadmap, and how to get involved with the CREDEBL and LFDT community.

title: Trusted AI Agents by Design: From Trust Ecosystems to Authority Continuity
description:
Rapid innovation in agentic AI is opening up real potential. But agents don't just forward intent, they create it. When an agent makes the decisions that matter, trust can't be assumed, it has to be designed in. And once agents cross organizational boundaries, decentralized trust infrastructure has a critical role to play.

This session brings together two complementary pieces tackling that fundamental challenge, followed by a panel. This is the timeframe to get things right. Join us.

**5:00 PM Opening & Framing** – Shane Deconinck

**5:10 PM Running AI Agent Protocols over Trust Spanning Protocol** – Wenjing Chu
How TMCP and TA2A bring secure, interoperable communication to AI agent ecosystems, built on the Trust Spanning Protocol.

**5:35 PM Authority Is Continuous** – Nicola Gallo
Introducing PIC (Provenance Identity Continuity Protocol) and its Proof of Continuity as an emerging security primitive for distributed transactions and agent chains.

**6:00 PM Closing Panel: Connecting the Layers** – Moderated by Shane Deconinck
We'll discuss how the proposed solutions fit together, which pieces are still missing, how they align with existing standards and ongoing work in the space, and what's needed to move from specification to adoption, with plenty of room for interaction.

title: O Futuro das Tecnologias Descentralizadas e o Protagonismo Brasileiro
description:
O Capítulo Brasil da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT) convida toda a comunidade tecnológica, desenvolvedores, entusiastas e tomadores de decisão para um encontro exclusivo com a liderança global da fundação.

Neste evento online e gratuito, discutiremos a evolução do ecossistema de confiança descentralizada. A LFDT vai além do Blockchain, englobando uma governança robusta para soluções de identidade digital, criptografia e infraestrutura de código aberto que fundamentam a economia digital moderna.

O que vamos abordar:

* Visão Global e Governança: Como a LFDT gerencia projetos críticos como Hyperledger Besu, Fabric, frentes de identidade digital entre outras soluções de código aberto para criação de redes de confiança decentralizada como é o modelo Web3.
* O Brasil como Protagonista: O país deixou de ser apenas um usuário de tecnologia para se tornar um ator relevante na contribuição e desenvolvimento do ecossistema global.
* Código Aberto vs. Lock-in Tecnológico: Por que o open source é a estratégia fundamental para países em desenvolvimento garantirem soberania digital e mitigarem a dependência de fornecedores únicos.
* Desafios e Oportunidades: As perspectivas da fundação para o próximo ano e onde estão as maiores janelas de inovação para profissionais e empresas brasileiras.

Este é um espaço aberto para troca de conhecimento, networking e para entender como você ou sua organização podem contribuir ativamente com a Linux Foundation.

## Apresentação da Palestrante

**Daniela Barbosa Diretora Executiva da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT)**

Daniela Barbosa é uma líder global no setor de tecnologia, com vasta experiência em ecossistemas de código aberto e inovação em enterprise blockchain. À frente da LFDT, ela coordena o desenvolvimento de padrões e tecnologias que sustentam a confiança digital em escala global. Com um olhar estratégico sobre a colaboração comunitária, Daniela tem sido uma ponte fundamental entre as demandas das grandes indústrias e a agilidade das comunidades de desenvolvedores, defendendo sempre o impacto positivo das tecnologias descentralizadas no crescimento econômico e na inclusão digital.

**Hart Montgomery, Diretor de Tecnologia da Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (LFDT)**

Hart possui vasta experiência em blockchain e criptografia, tendo atuado anteriormente em pesquisa nessas áreas na Fujitsu Research, onde ajudou a liderar os esforços da Fujitsu no Hyperledger. Antes da Fujitsu, Hart obteve seu doutorado em criptografia na Universidade de Stanford, sob a orientação de Dan Boneh, período em que foi bolsista de pós-graduação da instituição (Stanford Graduate Fellow). Hart conta com inúmeras publicações acadêmicas e patentes nas áreas de criptografia e blockchain, trazendo uma vasta experiência nesses domínios para a LF Decentralized Trust.

title: From Identity-First to Authority Continuity
description:
We built security around identity, tokens, and roles. It was never quite right, capability theorists knew this decades ago. AI agents just made the cracks impossible to ignore.

This is the moment to correct the model.

We will reason from first principles. What identity is. What an identifier is. What authority actually is, not a token you hold, but a continuous property of execution that can only shrink, never expand. Why confused deputy and privilege escalation are not edge cases. They are the structural outcome of building on possession.

We will work through the real delegation cases that break every IAM system built today, defined by Alan Karp, who has spent decades mapping them. Delegation and attenuation. Chained delegation across organizations. Revocation, including the hard case where you need to revoke someone you never delegated to directly. The confused deputy, known since 1988, still appearing in every generation of systems. Seven aspects of sharing that people rely on in the real world and that no identity-based, role-based, or attribute-based system handles correctly. The use cases are here: [alanhkarp.com/UseCases.pdf](http://alanhkarp.com/UseCases.pdf)

We will then explore how authority continuity changes everything. Moving from identity-first to an intent and execution model means authority is anchored at the origin, flows through a verifiable chain, and cannot be expanded, stolen, or reinterpreted at any hop.

AI agents are the opportunity we did not expect. Authority continuity is the correction we always needed.

title: Open Standards for Tokenization: Why Interoperability Matters
description:
Institutional adoption of tokenized assets depends on solving a critical infrastructure challenge: how can digital securities operate across multiple platforms, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes without recreating the vendor lock-in that has long limited legacy systems?

Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust and OpenAssets are helping establish this foundational layer through the Open Tokenized Asset Standard (OTAS), a recently approved lab focused on building protocol-agnostic standards for compliant, interoperable digital assets.

In this session, Surendra Kalidindi, CTO of OpenAssets, will start by exploring why open standards matter for institutional digital assets and how open approaches differ from proprietary tokenization platforms.

The session will be followed by a panel moderated by Daniela Barbosa, Executive Director of LF Decentralized Trust, featuring industry leaders from a global financial institution, a protocol engineering organization, and a provider of cross-chain and onchain data infrastructure. Together, they will discuss what the industry needs most to accelerate adoption, improve interoperability, and support real-world deployment at scale.

Join us to hear directly from industry leaders, learn more about initiatives like OTAS and the goals of the newly launched lab, and explore how institutions and developers can engage with the OTAS Lab, including a 2026 mentorship opportunity through LF Decentralized Trust.

🎤 CHARLA 1
Forecasting con intención: Cerrando la brecha entre algoritmos complejos y el valor para el usuario a través de UTE
Speaker: Marcelo Martínez
Empresa: Digital Sense
Descripción:
Existe una gran variedad de modelos de forecasting: desde regresiones lineales simples hasta modelos de transformers y generativos. Ante el avance del aprendizaje automático (ML), puede ser tentador recurrir a los modelos más sofisticados. Sin embargo, probar distintas arquitecturas y optimizar hiperparámetros puede resultar solo en mejoras marginales.
En su lugar, comprender a fondo las necesidades del cliente y traducirlas en acciones concretas durante el desarrollo del modelo puede generar resultados superiores. A través del caso de estudio sobre el pronóstico de la demanda eléctrica en Uruguay, analizaremos cómo abordar un problema de predicción desde una perspectiva holística, con el objetivo de desarrollar un sistema que sea preciso en el papel pero, sobre todo, útil para sus usuarios.
———————————————
🎤 CHARLA 2
Cómo ejecutar un roadmap cuando el futuro cambia cada semana (IA)
Speaker: Sebastián Galli
Empresa: Delto
Descripción:
Esta charla explora el desafío de ejecutar un roadmap de producto en un contexto donde la inteligencia artificial avanza a una velocidad que invalida supuestos en cuestión de meses. A partir de preguntas concretas, se analizará cómo decisiones y features que parecían estratégicos hace seis meses pueden volverse obsoletos hoy, y qué implica esto para la planificación, priorización y ejecución de producto. El foco estará en cómo adaptarse a este cambio constante: cuándo mantener el rumbo, cuándo pivotear, y cómo construir roadmaps más flexibles, iterativos y resilientes frente a la incertidumbre tecnológica.

*Un sistema de agentes no solo produce texto: también actúa. Y cuando falla, no falla «una frase», falla una decisión y eso puede disparar efectos secundarios inesperados (aprobar, enviar, borrar, etiquetar).*

*Todo esto entre una versión vulnerable y una versión corregida del mismo sistema. La idea es que te lleves algo valioso y aplicable en la práctica para tu laburo o proyecto personal.*

Quantum computing is no longer a distant threat. Improvements in hardware design, new algorithmic breakthroughs, and expert surveys now put a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer sooner than the industry is prepared for. Elliptic curve signatures and key exchange, RSA, and many ZK proof systems are vulnerable, where they underpin not just blockchains, but financial infrastructure, identity systems, enterprise software, and the internet itself.

However, the industry isn't standing still. In this workshop, Zain Cheng (CTO, Horizen Labs) and Tommaso Gagliardoni (Cryptography Research Manager, Horizen Labs) will give the LFDT community a comprehensive look at where the quantum migration stands today across blockchain ecosystems, traditional finance, government, and enterprise, and what you can do to prepare regardless of the stack you're building on.

The Threat Landscape: What quantum computers actually break, and what they don't. Shor's algorithm and elliptic curve cryptography. Grover's algorithm and symmetric/hash security. Why "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks make this urgent right now.

title: 🧉 Mate Talk | Latency vs. AI: The new Trade-off in Live Streaming

**Latency vs. AI: The New Trade-Off in Live Streaming**
For the last five years, live streaming has been in a latency arms race — sub-three seconds, sub-one second, glass-to-glass parity with broadcast. We've spent real engineering capital getting there.

Now AI is showing up in the same pipeline: live translation, real-time dubbing, AI-generated sign language, multilingual captioning. Each one adds processing time, buffer requirements, and packaging complexity.

The two priorities are pulling against each other, and the industry hasn't fully admitted it.

In this Mate Talk we'll dig into what that trade-off actually looks like in production.

Join us with **David Hassoun, Olga Kornienko, Bhavesh Upadhyaya, Sean McCarthy, Andy Beach, and our special guest Neal Roberts.**

Las comunidades, equipos y organizaciones enfrentan un desafío común:

**¿Cómo tomar decisiones sin depender siempre de las mismas personas?**

A medida que los grupos crecen, aparecen preguntas complejas:

* ¿Quién debería decidir?
* ¿Cómo distribuimos responsabilidades?
* ¿Cómo fomentamos la participación sin volvernos burocráticos?

En este encuentro de AgileUY vamos a explorar una propuesta que busca abordar estos desafíos: **la Sociocracia**.

La Sociocracia es un modelo de gobernanza que propone nuevas formas de organizarse, distribuir autoridad y tomar decisiones de manera más participativa y efectiva.

title: Increasing Trust on Ethereum with ENS and Enscribe
description:
Most organizations on Ethereum are effectively anonymous. Contracts are deployed to nameless addresses, treasury wallets have no verifiable link to the org that controls them, and AI agents operate with no on-chain accountability. For protocols and DAOs trying to build credibility and operate transparently, this is a real problem — and it's one that existing tooling hasn't solved.

In this webinar, we'll walk through how organizations can easily create and manage on-chain identity for everything they deploy, using ENS as the identity layer supported by Enscribe ([https://www.enscribe.xyz/](https://www.enscribe.xyz/)). We'll show how protocols can name and manage their smart contracts, wallets, and agents under a unified namespace, making their on-chain presence verifiable, human-readable, and auditable.

title: Architecture for Sustaining Open Source in Web 3
description:
Open source is the foundation of Web3, but most ecosystems still fund it like a series of short-term projects instead of long-term public infrastructure. As decentralized networks grow, the real challenge is no longer just building software. It is maintaining the critical code, tooling, standards, and contributor communities that keep the ecosystem secure, usable, and resilient.

This session explores what an architecture for sustaining open source in Web3 should look like. We will examine why traditional grant models often fall short, how maintenance differs from feature delivery, and why decentralized ecosystems need clearer coordination structures without recreating centralized control. The discussion will introduce models such as decentralized OSPOs and open maintenance frameworks as practical ways to align governance, funding, accountability, and contributor support.

Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of how Web3 ecosystems can move from reactive funding toward intentional stewardship of open source infrastructure.

title: Tech Meetup | "AI in Production: What's Actually Shipping in Media Workflows"
description:
Everyone's talking about AI in the media workflow — QoE optimization, multi-CDN decisioning, auto-cropping, clip and highlight generation. The demos look great. But the real question is: what's actually running in production?
That's the focus of our next Tech Meetup (Thu, July 30): not the pitch decks, but the practice, where AI is genuinely deployed in live media operations and content workflows, what broke on the way there, and what still keeps a human in the loop.

**Three talks. Three real projects. No pitch decks.**

#### 🔴 "Faster Answers Under Pressure: An AI Root-Cause Co-Pilot for Streaming Ops"

**Nicolás Caballero @ Qualabs**
When quality drops, the dashboard turns red. Explaining why is the hard part — complex diagnostic work under pressure. We'll share how we put an LLM in that loop: how to trust it at 3am when it's confident and wrong, how to keep it cost-effective, and where AI actually earns its place versus where it's just overhead.

#### ✂️ "Pass, Fail, or Ask a Human: AI Quality Control for Video at Scale"

**Emil Santurio @ Qualabs**
Producing highlights at scale means every clip needs a quality check before it airs. Clean cuts. Right moment. On-brand.
But here's the thing: quality isn't one thing. Some checks are mechanical rules. Some need you to actually look at the frame. Some are genuinely subjective and editorial.
The real challenge isn't "use AI" — it's knowing which tool fits each check. Pick the wrong one and you either miss errors or burn cost and trust.
We'll share the honest lessons from putting this into production: which checks we let code handle, which needed computer vision, which still need a human, and what we'd do differently.

#### 🌍 "From Voice to Subtitle to Sign Language"

**Alexander Leschinsky @ G&L**
Accessibility at scale isn't a feature — it's a workflow. Alexander is sharing how sign language (BSL, ASL, and now German Sign Language) is being integrated into professional live and on-demand encoding, subtitling, and delivery. Working with UK-based Signapse, putting sign language on equal footing with subtitles. The honest part: what works, what's harder than expected, and how it changes your infrastructure.

El segundo es **cuándo tiene sentido incorporar capacidades de IA dentro del producto para mejorar la propuesta de valor, y cuándo solo añade complejidad.**

Trabajar con IA exige experimentar, aprender rápido y tomar decisiones en un contexto de alta incertidumbre. Afortunadamente, esos son principios que la agilidad ha promovido desde siempre.

En esta meetup compartiremos aprendizajes y criterios prácticos para decidir qué vale la pena probar, qué adoptar y qué dejar pasar.

Porque el desafío ya no es usar IA por moda. Es utilizarla para construir mejores productos, tomar mejores decisiones y generar impacto.

title: 🧉 Mate Talk | "AI in Media: Your asset travels. Its context doesn't"
description:
🧉 Mate Talk is coming!

**AI in Media: Your Asset Travels. Its Context Doesn't.**
Every AI tool you plug into your media pipeline shows up knowing nothing about your library, and it stays that way. Your asset moves from tool to tool, handoff to handoff, but the context around it doesn't. It gets rebuilt from scratch every single time, so nothing ever compounds.

And there's a second layer to this that's less about the tools and more about us: we're generating 100-page docs with AI, then handing them straight back to AI to tell us what's in them, because nobody's actually going to read them. The knowledge exists somewhere. Our expertise doesn't grow.

So the real question: **how do you maintain and grow context and expertise in a world where the data and the tooling are temporary?**

Join us with **David Hassoun, Olga Kornienko, Bhavesh Upadhyaya, Sean McCarthy, Andy Beach, and JP Saibene**

title: 🎙️ Tech Meetup | C2PA on the road to IBC 2026!
description:
**C2PA on the Road to IBC 2026!**
Content authenticity is having a moment, AI-generated media, deepfakes, the growing question of "is this real?"
C2PA is the open standard trying to answer that: a cryptographically signed record of where a piece of media came from and whether it's been touched since.

That's the focus of our next Tech Meetup, ahead of IBC 2026: Qualabs and Unified Streaming sharing what we've actually been building on C2PA.

Our speakers:
**Pablo** **Flores** (VP of Engineering @ Qualabs) and **Valentijn Siebrands**
(@ Unified Streaming).

**Valentijn Talk \| "The Nutrition Label for Media: C2PA at the Packaging Stage"**
In the AI era, knowing where content comes from and whether it can be trusted matters more than ever.
C2PA acts like a modern “nutrition label” for media, carrying verifiable information about its origin and history. With Unified Streaming, those Content Credentials can be added dynamically at the packaging stage, for live and VOD — late enough to reflect the final stream, but early enough to preserve transparency before delivery.

Pablo Talk \| "**C2PA for Live Media, Upstream**
**Signing and validation in c2pa-rs, the Common Media Library, and dash.js"**
C2PA is an open, public spec, but the trip from reading it to running it across a real streaming pipeline is long - and for live, longer still. We made it and put the code where everyone can reach it: c2pa-rs, the SVTA Common Media Library, and dash.js. We'll show how to sign live video, how to validate it in the browser for live and VOD, and what's coming next.

title: Introducing the IPRAM Lab for Tokenized Regulated Asset Markets
description:
The tokenisation of regulated real-world assets has led to multiple institutional implementations of the same financial instruments, each operating on its own infrastructure with few shared patterns for how those infrastructures interoperate. As a result, tokenised assets remain confined to the environment they were issued in, accessible only to counterparties already inside the same institutional perimeter.

The IPRAM Lab ([https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM](https://github.com/LFDT-IPRAM)) develops open implementation patterns for the interoperation of tokenised real-world regulated financial assets and the markets they participate in. This session introduces the lab's mission, scope, and the initial interoperability challenges it aims to address. All interested parties are invited to join!

title: Migraciones de código legacy: potenciado el testing con IA
description:
Hoy en día, gracias al uso de asistentes de IA, se hizo más viable migrar sistemas legacy, como aplicaciones basadas en COBOL o RPG, a tecnologías modernas. Esto sucede gracias a que estos asistentes reducen costos del desarrollo al ayudar a entender el código legacy y regenerarlo en la nueva arquitectura. Sin embargo, el testing sigue siendo uno de los mayores obstáculos, especialmente porque en estos contextos la documentación es escasa o está desactualizada, y las personas con el conocimiento están poco disponibles o ya no están en la empresa, lo que dificulta verificar el comportamiento esperado.

En esta charla v**eremos una metodología que diseñamos en Abstracta para abordar este desafío con el apoyo de IA,** y veremos los aprendizajes que obtuvimos en los primeros proyectos realizando este tipo de migraciones. Esta metodología aborda el desafío como un problema de “characterization testing”, pudiendo generar cobertura en el sistema original a nivel de pruebas automatizadas y a nivel de pruebas funcionales a nivel de usuario. Esta cobertura se genera a partir del código y la documentación disponible, y se valida con las personas con conocimiento de negocio y desarrollo. Lo importante es poder generar outputs en ambas versiones del sistema que se puedan comparar, para encontrar diferencias en el comportamiento. A este enfoque se lo complementa con una comprensión dinámica a través de observabilidad. Presentamos cómo implementamos estos enfoques sobre Tero, nuestra plataforma open-source que desarrollamos para dar soporte a agentes de IA que asisten a los testers, y demostramos su uso con ejemplos concretos de un sistema COBOL.

Si bien todavía estamos recolectando métricas, los primeros resultados indican proyectos de migración más viables y beneficios tangibles al aplicar IA al testing. **Esta sesión propone repensar la IA como una aliada del tester, no solo del desarrollador.**

title: Open Source Climate Accounting: What Exists, What's Missing+Where To Contribute
description:
Climate accounting increasingly depends on systems that were never designed to work together. Registries use different standards and data models. The same activity can appear across multiple systems. Measurement data may come from sensors, satellite observations, models, or manual reporting, often with limited provenance or no straightforward way for downstream users to verify how a claim was produced.

These are not only reporting problems but they are problems of interoperability, provenance, reconciliation and trust between independent systems.

A substantial amount of open-source work already exists to address them, but much of it remains fragmented or little known outside the communities that built it. This session will map that landscape: what is already available, what is mature enough to use today, what remains experimental and where meaningful technical contributions are still needed.

The aim is not to argue that blockchain is the answer to climate accounting. It is to look practically at where distributed ledgers, verifiable data, open standards and other open-source infrastructure can solve specific problems or where they cannot.

Structure - The session would begin with a short framing of the technical problems behind climate and impact accounting: provenance, reconciliation, double counting, interoperability and verification across organisational boundaries.

From there, members of the LF Decentralized Trust community could walk through existing open-source projects and frameworks, explaining what they were built to solve, how mature they are and where they are being used today.

The final part would focus on the gaps: problems that remain unsolved, areas where maintainers would welcome contributions and practical ways for developers, researchers and organisations to get involved.

The IEEE ClimateChain Global Hackathon ([https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/](https://ieee-climatechain-hack.devpost.com/)) would be introduced as one of those routes to contribution.

The goal is for participants to leave with a clearer picture of what already exists, which problems are genuinely open and where their time and technical skills could have the greatest value.

title: Policy-Checked, Attributable, Revocable, Provable AI Agent Authorization
description:
AI agents are entering production with long-lived API keys in their environment, broader access than any task needs, and no answer to the questions: Which agent performed this action? Under whose authority?

A single prompt injection, leaked credential, or runaway agent can quickly become a security incident. Security reviews delay deployments, and auditors are often left without sufficient evidence to understand what happened.

Existing security infrastructure was not designed for autonomous AI agents. Identity providers register agents but do not authorize every action, secret managers distribute credentials to workloads, and API gateways route requests without making authorization decisions.

This talk introduces Caracal, an open source AI authorization system currently being developed through the LFDT LFX Mentorship program and supported by GitHub, Microsoft, and Vercel. We'll discuss what authority means for AI agents, why authorization must move beyond credentials, and how we designed Caracal's architecture to provide policy-based authorization, attribution, revocation, and auditability for agent actions.

The session will cover:

* Why traditional API key and identity models are insufficient for AI agents
* What authority means in autonomous AI systems
* The architectural design behind Caracal
* Practical approaches to securing AI agents in production

The meetup will be presented by the Caracal team, Ryan Madhuwala and Shubham Sharma.

Our LFX mentees, Mohammad Ali Haider and Ashutosh Singh, will also present their work on the project. If you're interested in AI security and secure agent infrastructure, we'd be happy to have you join us.

title: AI × Decentralized Trust: Kickoff of the LFDT AI Working Group
description:
AI is already in our pull requests — and agentic AI needs exactly what we build. Let's talk about both.

AI has already arrived in our repositories. It writes patches, reviews pull requests, and is often the first thing a newcomer asks about a codebase they don't understand yet. At the same time, agentic AI is arriving from the other direction — as a use case. Autonomous agents need identities they can prove, credentials others can verify, and a way to pay each other for the things they consume. That is our home turf.

LFDT has no shared position on either side of this yet. This meeting launches the LFDT AI Working Group and sets its scope together with the people who will do the work.

We will open three questions:

**How do we use AI when building LFDT projects? What** is allowed, what has to be disclosed, and what does it mean for provenance, licensing, DCO sign-off, and security review? The Linux Foundation's existing generative AI guidance is the floor — the question is what our projects need on top of it.

**Can AI help us grow our communities?** Review bots like CodeRabbit, automated triage of good first issues, and onboarding assistants promise a shorter path from first-time contributor to committer. Do they actually deliver that, or do they just add noise for maintainers to clean up? And if we want them, who runs them and who pays?

**Where does our work connect to the AI world?** Two neighbours at the Linux Foundation matter most: the Agentic AI Foundation (MCP, goose, AGENTS.md) and the x402 Foundation, which stewards payments over HTTP for agents. Agentic identity and agent-to-agent commerce are exactly where DLT belongs — and where LFDT projects should be visible.

This is a kickoff, not a keynote. Bring your opinions, your objections, and the problems you already have. We want to leave with an initial scope, a meeting cadence, and named volunteers for the first work streams.

Open to everyone: maintainers, contributors, TSC members, LFDT staff, and anyone from the wider Linux Foundation AI ecosystem. No prior involvement in LFDT required.

title: ConnectIA 2026
summary:
Tercera edición de **ConnectIA**, la conferencia gratuita de inteligencia artificial y ciencia de datos de Uruguay, pensada para profesionales, académicos y estudiantes. Está anunciada para el sábado 31 de octubre de 2026 en el **Auditorio del LATU**, en Montevideo: una jornada completa de charlas magistrales, casos de uso reales y networking, con entrada libre previa inscripción.

El llamado a charlas estuvo abierto en Sessionize del 12 de agosto al 20 de septiembre de 2026. Se pedían casos de estudio, modelos en producción, LLMs y agentes, MLOps, ética e investigación, en charlas de 30 minutos más 10 de preguntas y sin contenido comercial. La organización iba a anunciar la grilla de oradores después de evaluar las propuestas.

La sostienen sponsors como GeneXus Consulting, Blend360, Marvik, SunnyData, Xmartlabs, Ingenio, la Universidad de Montevideo y la Universidad ORT Uruguay. Las ediciones anteriores, en 2024 y 2025, tuvieron charlas sobre evaluación de LLMs, IA en diagnóstico médico, agricultura, educación y sistemas de recomendación. La primera superó los 300 asistentes.

title: OWU CONF 2026

sources.label: OWU CONF en owu.uy (programa, speakers y entradas)

summary:
Primera edición de **OWU CONF**, la conferencia de la comunidad tecnológica uruguaya que organiza OWU. Es la continuación de La Meetup, que se hizo de 2023 a 2025, ahora en formato de conferencia y con el mismo espíritu. Está prevista para el sábado 7 de noviembre de 2026 en Sinergia Faro (Víctor Soliño 349, Montevideo), de 14:30 a 20:40. Las entradas se liberaron el miércoles 14 de octubre a las 11:00.

El programa anunciado arranca con acreditación y bienvenida, y sigue con un **open space**: a las 15:15 el mercado de ideas, donde cualquiera puede proponer un tema, y de 16:00 a 18:25 cinco bloques de sesiones simultáneas. Después del coffee break vienen dos charlas de cierre, la foto de toda la comunidad y un after:

- **Retrieval Augmented Gaslight**, de Sebastián Passaro (OWASP Uruguay), sobre cómo un solo documento envenenado alcanza para engañar a un chatbot con RAG y cómo defenderse con herramientas open source.
- **Kingdom Rush Battles: del lanzamiento al live ops**, de Juan Pais y Ciro Mondueri (Ironhide Game Studio), sobre cómo llevaron Kingdom Rush a su primer juego multijugador y de operación continua.
